metadata.title: Research on personalized assessment Information of students’ mathematical competency based on cognitive diagnosis

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses TIMSS 2015 Grade 8 mathematics items to build a cognitive diagnosis assessment for students sampled from four mainland China provinces/cities (Gansu, Guizhou, Guangdong, Shanghai). The manuscript does not report the use of TIMSS sampling/survey weights or any replicate-weight scheme, nor does it name weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or describe complex-survey variance estimation. Because the analysis is based on cognitive diagnosis models (CDMs) and model comparison using fit indices (AIC/BIC/RMSEA2) rather than standard ML prediction with explicit survey-weighted estimation, the paper provides no guidance on how to weight students to represent the underlying population. For replication with TIMSS microdata, analysts should apply the official TIMSS student sampling weights and replicate weights (if available) when estimating uncertainty, and should document any exclusions (e.g., incomplete learning-path coverage) that may affect representativeness.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This study is a cognitive diagnosis assessment using cognitive diagnosis models (e.g., DINA/DINO/RRUM/ACDM/LLM/LCDM/Mixed Model) to infer mastery of eight attributes from item responses, rather than predicting PV-based cognitive achievement scores. As a result, plausible values (PV) are not the target quantity in the analysis pipeline. The manuscript also does not describe any explicit missing-data strategy (e.g., complete-case selection, imputation, or model-based handling), so the missing-data handling is a reporting gap rather than a clearly defined design choice.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample for the cognitive diagnosis tool is 4,733 Grade 8 students from four mainland China provinces/cities: Gansu, Guizhou, Guangdong, and Shanghai, using TIMSS 2015 Grade 8 mathematics test items. For the learning-path analysis, the paper reports that the knowledge-state learning path in Fig. 3 includes 4,444 students and that 289 students were not included in the learning path, implying an additional filtering criterion for learning-path construction (e.g., knowledge-state coverage/representation). Beyond these reported exclusions for the learning-path figure, the manuscript does not specify further inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., item nonresponse thresholds, missing background-variable rules, or complete-case criteria).

main_findings.dataset_used: TIMSS 2015 Grade 8 Mathematics (mainland China sample; four provinces/cities)
main_findings.target_variable: Personalized diagnostic report recommendations (attribute mastery + follow-up sequences)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Four example students’ diagnostic report cards are provided (GZBS051, GSLS252, GDZD451, SHYH026). The paper reports recommended follow-up learning sequences derived from each student’s knowledge status and the learning path (e.g., GZBS051: Number Crunching→Shape Operation→While Generalization; SHYH026: Shape Operation→Proportional Reasoning→Data analysis & evaluation→Functional Idea→Algebraic Transformation). Additional analysis (Learning progression levels (five-level ability intervals) and distribution): Competency values: smallest knowledge state (00000000) ability=-1.67; largest (11111111) ability=0.60. Learning progression divided into 5 levels from -1.75 to 0.75 with step 0.5. Distribution: most knowledge states fall in levels 2 and 3, some in level 4; only one knowledge state in level 1 and one in level 5. Additional analysis (Learning path coverage and main knowledge-state sequence): Learning path in Fig. 3 includes 4,444 students; 289 students not included; coverage rate=93.9%. Main learning path sequence reported: (00000000)→(00010000)→(00011000)→(00011100)→(00011101)→(01011101)→(11011101)→(11111101)→(11111111). Additional analysis (Attribute mastery probabilities (eight basic mathematics skills)): Model comparison (CDMs): Mixed Model best fit by AIC/BIC (AIC=14848.97; BIC=16228.02) and absolute fit RMSEA2=0.0348 (<0.05). Reliability: Cronbach’s alpha=0.9079; attribute reliabilities range 0.9100–0.9935 (SR=0.946). Group differences (chi-square): Mainland China shows significant advantages for most attributes vs Singapore/Japan/Korea/Taiwan/Hong Kong (p-values reported in Table 5).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TIMSS 2015 Grade 8 Mathematics the study leveraged attribute mastery probabilities and the inferred learning path to generate personalized diagnostic report recommendations, finding that students with the same overall score can be located at different learning progression levels and therefore receive different follow-up attribute sequences. This indicates that schools can use cognitive diagnosis outputs to design individualized remediation and resource allocation, improving alignment between student readiness and next-step instruction.

data.outcome_summary: This study uses TIMSS 2015 Grade 8 mathematics test items to construct a cognitive diagnosis assessment framework with eight basic mathematics attributes (NC, AT, SO, SR, PR, FI, WG, DE). The main empirical dataset is 4,733 Grade 8 students from four mainland China provinces/cities (Gansu, Guizhou, Guangdong, Shanghai), and the paper also compares attribute mastery against Singapore, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, and Hong Kong using the same TIMSS-based attribute framework. For model selection, the Mixed Model is chosen as best fit using AIC/BIC (AIC=14848.97; BIC=16228.02) and absolute fit RMSEA2=0.0348 (<0.05), with high reliability (Cronbach’s alpha=0.9079; attribute reliabilities mostly >0.91). The learning path covers 93.9% of students (4,444 included; 289 excluded) and suggests a dominant progression beginning with Spatial Reasoning. Limitations include the lack of reported missing-data handling and the fact that the “learning path/progression” is constructive and not yet validated in practice.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The manuscript is primarily a cognitive diagnosis assessment construction and model-comparison study (CDMs and a Mixed Model) rather than a machine-learning predictive modeling paper with supervised targets and reported ML metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC). Consequently, no ML predictive algorithms are extracted into ml_techniques, and main_findings focus on diagnostic attribute mastery, learning-path/progression construction, and personalized report outputs. The paper also does not report a missing-data strategy, so missing_data_handling is set to not_reported.
